lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Clarify what “owned” means and what you built or maintained.
items.because: The bullet establishes responsibility but not your technical contribution or its impact.

items.says: Add a concrete result if you can substantiate one.
items.because: Without a result, the bullet is less compelling than the others.

items.says: Explain the load-test traffic, environment, measurement period, and comparison conditions.
items.because: Readers need to know whether the before-and-after figures were measured under the same conditions.

items.says: State what the 200 ms build threshold applies to and how it relates to the 180 ms result.
items.because: That would make the test safeguard easier to interpret.

items.says: Clarify how the regression checks contributed to shorter release cycles.
items.because: The causal link is plausible but not demonstrated.

items.says: Define “release cycle” and how the two-week and three-day figures were measured.
Split or narrow the bullet’s many responsibilities.
items.because: Combining them makes your contribution and the reason for the backlog improvement hard to assess.

items.says: Clarify the event-queue migration’s scope and outcome, separating it from onboarding and on-call work.
Explain what “removed the nightly backlogs” means operationally and how you verified it.
Clarify whether “branch” means a code branch, product capability, or workflow.
items.because: The term is ambiguous here.

items.says: Define the 68% backlog reduction’s baseline and calculation, and address other possible contributing changes.
Specify the deployment setting, your role, and what “after launch” means.
items.because: Those details would make the result stronger.

items.says: Give the model or baseline, data-split procedure, and independence of the 1,200 held-out cases.
items.because: The accuracy result needs evaluation context to be defensible.

items.says: Explain why accuracy is suitable for the task, especially if classes are imbalanced.
Clarify what the domain adapter and assistant-only loss masking did technically.
items.because: These specialized claims are likely interview targets.

items.says: Explain how dynamic batching affected p95 latency for “single-request” inference.
items.because: The two descriptions appear to be in tension without workload and measurement conditions.

items.says: Identify the baseline and device or deployment environment.
items.because: Without them, the 40% improvement is difficult to compare or reproduce.

items.says: Rewrite the sentence fragment as a complete description of your contribution.
Add evaluation context for the 5% latency reduction.
Explain how the reward components were combined.
Clarify whether lower latency affected accuracy or citation validity.
items.because: A composite reward makes that trade-off especially relevant.

items.says: Distinguish your implementation or experiments from the overall training setup.
Resolve how one scored trajectory per prompt fits a GRPO method.
items.because: GRPO ordinarily uses multiple responses per prompt to calculate group-relative advantages.

items.says: Explain what “grouped” means, how the advantage or baseline was computed, and how this method differs from standard GRPO if applicable.
items.because: The review says the evidence for calling the procedure GRPO is unclear.

items.says: Give a measurable indication of what “Stabilised” means.
items.because: The claim needs a defined training-failure or variance measure.

items.says: Clarify whether you defined the abstention rules or documented them, and what reviewer adoption meant.
Include evidence of an operational benefit if there is one, or present this as a documentation contribution.
items.because: The bullet should not imply an unmeasured outcome.

items.says: Support or remove the claims about faster delivery and better outcomes.
items.because: They are broad claims without a metric, example, or defined scope.

items.says: Clarify what “drove adoption” means and who adopted the practices.
The stated 50% latency reduction is incorrect; 900 ms to 600 ms is a 33.3% reduction.
Specify benchmark conditions, including whether task mix and cache behavior matched before and after.
The change from 71% to 83% is 12 percentage points, not a 12% relative increase.
Describe the benchmark size, evaluation procedure, and whether the result held across repeated runs.
Address latency, cost, or reliability trade-offs from retries with partial context.
Make the upstream and every-release benchmark claims verifiable through public contributions or documentation.
Clarify what you implemented versus what others reviewed or merged.
items.because: Open-source ownership matters for some roles.

items.says: Explain the two variables in the Kendall correlation and how the 400-plus trials were constructed.
Clarify how removing citations, sources, and claims defined the degradation tests.
items.because: Reproducible degradation levels and procedures would support a stronger claim.

items.says: Explain how tracing the defects enabled their fixes.
items.because: The bullet says you traced defects and they were fixed, but not how your work connected the two.

items.says: Substantiate the three fixes with issue or pull-request references and distinguish diagnoses from fixes you authored.
Separate infrastructure tools from ML and agent topics.
items.because: Kubernetes among ML and agent skills makes the categories less clear.

items.says: Reconcile the GRPO skill with the one-rollout claim if you list it.
items.because: You should be able to explain the method’s implementation.

items.says: Check that the linked code profile is accessible.
items.because: It may contain the projects or contributions cited on the résumé.

items.says: Check that project claims match what is visible on the linked code profile.
Consider adding substantiated graduate coursework or academic work relevant to a target role.
items.because: It should help match the role, not just fill space.

items.says: Expand the short skills list with relevant tools and technologies you can discuss in depth.
items.because: The list is short relative to the experience described.

items.says: Put the more recent Mobility Systems internship before the 2022–2024 role.
items.because: Experience is currently ordered in the wrong chronological direction.

items.says: Check and be ready to explain the concurrent 2025 internship and project dates.
Avoid line wrapping that splits “on-call” awkwardly.
items.because: The review says this happens in the pasted text.
